blocks.text: The reactivity of Group 2 elements follows from their electronic configuration. They lose their two outer electrons (ns2) to form stable M2+ ions, which makes them react readily. Reactivity increases from beryllium to barium because the atoms grow larger, shielding increases and the ionization energy decreases, so the electrons are removed more easily.

blocks.alt: Five Group 2 elements, Be, Mg, Ca, Sr and Ba, each drawn as a red half-sphere (the atom) over a smaller blue half-sphere (its M2+ ion). Both grow steadily from beryllium to barium.
blocks.caption: Figure 17.1: Relative sizes of the atoms of the Group 2 elements (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 17.1).
blocks.long_description: From left to right the elements are beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium and barium. Each red half-sphere is larger than the one before it, and so is the blue half-sphere below it.

blocks.title: Reactivity series of Group 2
blocks.text: Be < Mg < Ca < Sr < Ba: beryllium is the least reactive and barium the most reactive element of the group.
